scope: Compatibility bridge for the newest unconsumed canonical-main Triggerword-5 research-projection runs: stern effect-path lineage, ingest-path drift, and hook invocation identity. High-impact invocation/enforcement claims were cross-checked against exact donor source and current Anthropic Claude Code hook documentation; historical runtime claims remain historical claims only.

atoms.what_it_does: zulassen() creates a new effect_id and stores it in active_turns.effect_id selected only by session_id. The inspected donor repository contains no tool_use_id reference. Current Claude Code primary hook documentation exposes tool_use_id on tool-hook input and documents parallel tool batches/PostToolUse concurrency. The donor therefore discards an available call-scoped identity and relies on a weaker mutable session-scoped pointer.
atoms.why_it_exists: The donor evolved a two-phase pre/post effect journal before exact per-invocation correlation was made an explicit architecture invariant.
atoms.failure_mode: If same-session state-changing tool invocations overlap, a later PreToolUse can overwrite the session-wide pointer before an earlier PostToolUse reads it. Runtime manifestation is not claimed without a trace.
atoms.concurrency_implication: Per-invocation identity is required; session_id alone is contextual identity, not an exact effect correlation key.
atoms.latency_or_cost_implication: Using the already-present hook call identity should add negligible overhead compared with mutable-slot repair/reconciliation.
atoms.state_lifetime: session mutable pointer plus durable effect rows
tests_or_receipts: Anthropic Claude Code hooks reference observed 2026-08-28: tool_use_id on PreToolUse input; PostToolBatch after parallel tool calls; PostToolUse fires per tool
known_counterevidence: The exact installed host scheduler might serialize the relevant calls; this could bound present runtime risk but would not make a session-wide mutable pointer a sound Frankenstein-2.0 identity contract.
open_questions: Capture exact installed-version same-session parallel tool trace if runtime discrimination is later authorized.
Bind tool_use_id or successor invocation_id through admission, execution, outcome, re-entry and completion receipts.

atoms.what_it_does: cmd_hook can emit permissionDecision=deny for the session-bound DIGITAL-SEBUKKU condition. In the ordinary PreToolUse path it calls zulassen() and deliberately emits no deny/block response. Thus the hook surface can enforce a block, but the donor's ordinary named EffectGate bookkeeping does not exercise that host capability.
atoms.why_it_exists: SEBUKKU is a separate session-termination invariant; ordinary effect bookkeeping was designed fail-open/nonblocking in this donor phase.
outputs: deny only for SEBUKKU, otherwise bookkeeping side effects
writes: effects via zulassen on normal path
atoms.failure_mode: Architecture prose that says there is no PreToolUse deny anywhere is stale/overbroad; architecture prose that treats zulassen as the real blocking EffectGate is also false for this donor SHA.
tests_or_receipts: Anthropic Claude Code hooks reference: permissionDecision=deny prevents tool call
known_counterevidence: A separate host-only wache-koenig predecessor may enforce additional policy; its exact source remains unresolved provenance.
open_questions: Acquire or explicitly mark unavailable the host-only wache-koenig artifact.

atoms.what_it_does: merken() can synthesize a new effects row as VERIFIED after a successful PostToolUse when no PreToolUse row exists. VERIFIED therefore encodes observed post-tool success in at least one path without proving prior admission.
atoms.why_it_exists: The donor explicitly prefers a non-empty post-effect journal when PreToolUse bookkeeping timed out or failed.
atoms.failure_mode: Downstream consumers can over-credit VERIFIED as admitted-and-verified when it may only mean posthoc observed success.
atoms.concurrency_implication: The fallback also illustrates why exact per-call identity must survive missing pre-admission records.
known_counterevidence: An external host gate could have authorized the call; that authorization is not established by this effects row/status itself.
open_questions: Audit every downstream effects.status consumer before migration.

hypotheses: The historical in-process voice transition, configuration-cache lifetime failure, outcome-payload drop and schema-drift reports are architecture-relevant lineage evidence for explicit generation/freshness and field-complete re-entry contracts, but remain historical/runtime-receipt claims until independently reproduced or exact-currently revalidated.

Frankenstein 2.0 should use an immutable tool_use_id or generated invocation_id across ADMISSION_DECISION -> ENFORCEMENT_DECISION -> EXECUTION_RECEIPT -> WORLD_EFFECT_VERIFICATION -> RESULT_REENTRY -> COMPLETION_EVIDENCE.
counterhypotheses: The installed host may serialize relevant same-session state-changing tool invocations; this can reduce immediate donor race exposure but does not remove the structural identity weakness.
The unresolved host-only wache-koenig may already be the true blocking effect authority; only exact source/host evidence can establish that lineage.
contradictions: TW5-CONTRADICTION-INGEST-PATH-001 remains open: canonical main architecture_archaeology feed and owner-branch frankenstein_architecture_ingest inbox/state are both active research projections and are not silently aliased.

TW5-CONTRADICTION-EFFECT-ENFORCEMENT-003: donor comments say no PreToolUse deny exists anywhere, while current cmd_hook contains an explicit SEBUKKU deny; normal effect admission is nevertheless deliberately nonblocking.
TW5-CONTRADICTION-VERIFIED-PREADMISSION-004: VERIFIED can be synthesized without a PreToolUse row, so observed outcome and prior admission are not structurally separated by effects.status.

TW5-CONTRADICTION-INVOCATION-IDENTITY-005: the host hook protocol exposes a call-scoped tool_use_id and parallel tool semantics, while donor effect correlation uses one mutable session-scoped active_turns.effect_id.
